paragraphs.title: The Day of Calamity for Egypt and Its Neighbors

easy.explanation: The prophet was told to say, “Howl ye, Woe worth the day!” and the day of the Lord was near.
easy.q: What was the prophet commanded to proclaim?

easy.explanation: The passage calls it “a cloudy day” and says it will be the time of the heathen.
easy.q: What kind of day is described as being near?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “the sword shall come upon Egypt.”
easy.q: Which land is specifically said to be struck by the sword?

answers: Great pain would come upon it
medium.explanation: The passage says that great pain would be in Ethiopia when the slain fell in Egypt.
medium.q: What would happen in Ethiopia when the slain fell in Egypt?

medium.explanation: The expression describes the distress and terror caused by Egypt’s fall.
medium.q: In this passage, what does “great pain” describe?

answers: They would fall with Egypt by the sword
They would willingly leave the land
They would build cities in Egypt
medium.explanation: Ethiopia, Libya, Lydia, Chub, and others are said to fall with Egypt by the sword.
medium.q: Why would Egypt’s allies and neighboring peoples fall with it?

answers: Egypt’s destruction would cause Ethiopia to be afraid
Ethiopia would protect Egypt from destruction
Egypt’s destruction would make Ethiopia confident
challenge.explanation: Messengers would go forth to make the careless Ethiopians afraid, and great pain would come upon them.
challenge.q: What connection does the passage make between Egypt’s destruction and Ethiopia’s reaction?

answers: It would be a day of judgment and national downfall
It would be a day of peaceful trade
It would be a quiet gathering of nations
challenge.explanation: The cloud, sword, and falling nations point to a day of judgment and calamity.
challenge.q: What does the phrase “a cloudy day; it shall be the time of the heathen” suggest about the day?

answers: They would become desolate and wasted
They would remain as strong as before
They would receive help from every nation
challenge.explanation: Egypt’s helpers would be destroyed, and its cities would be among the cities that were wasted.
challenge.q: What overall result is described for Egypt and its cities?

paragraphs.title: The Destruction of Egypt, Its Cities, and Its Centers

easy.explanation: The Lord said that the multitude of Egypt would cease by the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon.
easy.q: By whose hand would the multitude of Egypt cease?

easy.explanation: They would be brought to destroy the land and would draw their swords against Egypt.
easy.q: What would Nebuchadrezzar and his people do to the land?

easy.explanation: The Lord said, “I will make the rivers dry.”
easy.q: What would happen to the rivers?

answers: The land would become more prosperous
The rivers would bring military protection
medium.explanation: The dry rivers are part of the desolation and destruction coming upon Egypt.
medium.q: What does the drying of the rivers show about Egypt’s condition?

medium.explanation: The Lord said He would destroy Egypt’s idols and cause its images to cease.
medium.q: In the context of the passage, what are “idols” and “images” associated with?

answers: They would fall by the sword, and the cities would go into captivity
They would become rulers of Egypt
They would lead Egypt to victory
medium.explanation: The young men would fall by the sword, and the cities would go into captivity.
medium.q: What would happen to the young men of Aven and Pibeseth?

answers: Babylon’s army comes, the land is destroyed, the rivers dry up, and people go into captivity
The cities prosper, the rivers increase, and the captives return
Egypt defeats Babylon and restores its cities
challenge.explanation: The verses describe Babylon’s invasion, the land’s destruction, dry rivers, and captivity.
challenge.q: Which sequence best summarizes the destruction described in these verses?

answers: The judgment would affect many important centers in Egypt
Only one city would be affected
The cities would defend Egypt successfully
challenge.explanation: Several Egyptian cities and centers are named as suffering fire, judgment, sword, or captivity.
challenge.q: What does the list of cities such as No, Sin, Noph, Zoan, and Tehaphnehes emphasize?

answers: They would know that the Lord is God
They would appoint a new Egyptian king
challenge.explanation: The passage concludes, “they shall know that I am the Lord.”
challenge.q: What spiritual result is stated at the end of the passage?

paragraphs.title: The Breaking of Pharaoh's Military Power

easy.explanation: The Lord said, “I have broken the arm of Pharaoh king of Egypt.”
The Lord said, “I will strengthen the arms of the king of Babylon.”
easy.q: Whose arms would the Lord strengthen?

answers: They would rule over the nations
easy.explanation: The Lord said He would scatter the Egyptians among the nations and disperse them through the countries.
easy.q: What would happen to the Egyptians among the nations?

medium.explanation: The arm is connected with holding a sword and exercising power in battle.
medium.q: What does Pharaoh’s arm represent in this passage?

medium.explanation: The image describes Pharaoh’s anguish and helplessness before Babylon.
medium.q: What does Pharaoh’s groaning like a deadly wounded man communicate?

answers: Babylon’s king is strengthened while Pharaoh’s arms fall down
Pharaoh is strengthened while Babylon’s king falls
medium.explanation: The passage repeatedly contrasts the strengthening of Babylon’s king with the breaking of Pharaoh’s arms.
medium.q: How are the conditions of Babylon’s king and Pharaoh contrasted?

answers: Pharaoh’s power is broken, while Babylon’s power is strengthened
Both kings surrender their swords willingly
Pharaoh’s power grows while Babylon becomes weak
challenge.explanation: The central contrast is the breaking of Egypt’s power and the strengthening of Babylon’s king.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast in the description of the two military powers?

answers: Babylon’s victory would be part of the act by which people would know the Lord
The sword would prevent the Lord’s judgment
The sword has no connection with knowing the Lord
challenge.explanation: The passage says they would know the Lord when He put His sword into the hand of Babylon’s king.
challenge.q: What is the connection between giving the sword to Babylon’s king and knowing the Lord?

answers: Egypt itself would be scattered among the nations and countries
Egypt would remain gathered in its own land
challenge.explanation: The prophecy concerns not only Pharaoh’s defeat but also the scattering of the Egyptians.
challenge.q: What important detail might be missed if one focuses only on Pharaoh’s broken arms?
